beats.text: Five books that were banned — and are absolutely worth reading.
One. Huckleberry Finn — Twain. Banned again and again, yet one of the great American novels.
Two. Ulysses — Joyce. Put on trial for obscenity; now a pillar of modern literature.
Three. Leaves of Grass — Whitman. Called filthy in its day for simply celebrating the body and the self.
Four. The Canterbury Tales — Chaucer. Censored for centuries for being far too rude and too honest.
Five. Frankenstein — Shelley. Banned as blasphemous for daring to ask who really plays God.
The books people try hardest to silence are usually the ones most worth hearing.
